Fantastic gastronomic experience
Apr 2022
We were passing through HCMC and decided it was a great opportunity to experience a world famous Kobe beef steak. On arrival we were escorted to our room and allocated a dedicated server who took our order. We opted for a Kobe set menu and a Foie Gras set menu. In the UK this would be called a fine dining tasting menu Our allocated chef appeared and set up to prepare the meal on the hot plate in front of us.
The Foie Gras menu included courses of prawns, scallops, salmon, foie gras and Australian rib eye. See photos. The skill and hand speed of our chef was phenomenal as she cooked and prepared the various courses. The Kobe was melt in the mouth special. The textures, flavours and presentation of all the dishes are up there with some Michelin starred restaurants I have visited.
Sitting at a table with a chef preparing food at the table may not suit anyone looking for a quiet intimate experience. But we found it to be a fantastic gastronomic experience. Fabulous.

Not a good Teppanyaki experience
Jun 2017 • Business
Sorry to say that it didn't live up to our expectation. 

We had not reserve any seats because we just found the comment from TripAdvisor was not bad, therefore we walked in to try this restaurant.
After waited about 5-10mins, staff arranged a private room to us. 
Staff were nice.
We ordered 2 sets for 2person, one Kobe beef set VN660,000 & one salmon set VN620,000.
We were disappointed by the cooking way of the chief because all dishes were too oily and lack of original flavour of the ingredients. 
The ingredients they used were not bad. Traditional Teppanyaki should be cooking in a fast and accurate way, however we just experienced a rush dinner with seeing the chief killing the prawn awkwardly.
We tried Teppanyaki in Japan, Hong Kong, Taiwan which were good and traditional, but for this restaurant in HCMC, ummmmm.... sorry to say, we will not come next time.

Top quality meal
Jan 2017 • Family
We love teppanyaki, but rarely have it when at home as it is hellishly expensive. 

We were pleasantly surprised when we visited Kobe Teppanyaki. The food was wonderful and very plentiful. 3 of our part had the American Rib menu, whilst I had the Aussie Beef menu. All in, each menu had 7 courses plus an ice cream dessert, as well as a bottomless cup of tea. Our bill was an affordable AUD170.00 for the four meals - approx one third what a similar Melbourne restaurant would cost. 

You don't get the theatrics, such as flames and egg tossing that some restaurants may offer. But, the staff were pleasant and attentive, and the manager was pleased to personally arrange a cab ride back to our hotel for us. (Which cost around $3 AU)

If you love Teppanyaki, this is a great place to visit.

Delightful--Elegant--Impressive--Beyond Belief
Mar 2015 • Couples
Kobe, thank you for putting the "F" back in food. I driven past this restaurant many times in Ho Chi Minh City. Finally, I stopped and made reservations. We ordered the Kobe beef and a rib eye cooked medium rare. The food was prepared teppanyaki style in front of us. I might add the food was served in courses like they do in Europe. We started with salad, miso soup, and then the entrees. The beef literally melted in my mouth. I observed my guest as she put the beef in her mouth. Her eyes popped and suddenly she looked at me with a big delightful smile radiated on her face. The food came in about 6 timely courses included grilled salmon cooked in a special wine sauce. Service was impeccable to say the least the cook chef was friendly and beautiful spoke very good English as she entertained the couples sitting around the grill. You will enjoy their friendly, welcoming atmosphere along with Japanese decorated surroundings. The soft, gentle lighting along with a wonderful fresh breeze blew in from the windows created a thought provoking ambiance. Costs: This restaurant is very expensive but in my opinion I left thinking I owed them more money. Because it has been years since I had a dining experience equal to this. I think all things considered you have to pay for a culinary experience like this. The last time I had food like this was in the eighties in Belgium and there we were serenaded by a violinist during the meal. I guess this comes down to one thing. "you have to pay to play." Thanks Kobe for bringing more meaning to my food life. I feel alive again. Please make reservations.
